recipes.title: Classic Red Borscht
recipes.description: A vibrant and nutrient-dense beet soup that is a staple of Russian cuisine. Packed with root vegetables and high in antioxidants, it's both healthy and deeply satisfying.
instructions: In a large pot, sauté the onions and carrots until golden. Add the shredded cabbage and potatoes.
Add 8 cups of water or vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
In a separate skillet, sauté the grated beets with tomato paste and lemon juice for 10 minutes. This preserves the bright red color.
Add the beet mixture to the main pot. Simmer for another 30 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Serve hot with a dollop of non-fat Greek yogurt and fresh dill.

recipes.title: Buckwheat Kasha with Sautéed Mushrooms
recipes.description: Buckwheat (Grechka) is a powerhouse of nutrition in Russia. This savory porridge is high in fiber and minerals, paired with earthy mushrooms for a complete healthy meal.
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat groats. Combine with 2 cups of water and a pinch of salt in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15-18 minutes until the water is absorbed.
While the buckwheat cooks, sauté onions and mushrooms in a non-stick skillet until golden brown.
Fluff the buckwheat with a fork and stir in the mushroom mixture. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Lite Beef Stroganoff over Buckwheat
recipes.description: A healthy variation of the world-famous Russian dish. We use lean beef sirloin and replace heavy cream with high-protein Greek yogurt for a rich but light sauce.
instructions: Sear the beef strips in a hot pan until browned. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onions and mushrooms in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Whisk together the Greek yogurt and mustard. Turn the heat to the lowest setting.
Return the beef to the pan and stir in the yogurt mixture. Warm through for 1 minute (do not boil).
Serve over cooked buckwheat or whole wheat noodles.

recipes.title: Vinegret (Root Vegetable Salad)
recipes.description: A traditional beet and pickle salad. This colorful dish is a great source of fiber and probiotics from the fermented pickles, finished with a light oil dressing.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the diced beets, potatoes, carrots, and pickles.
Add the green peas and 1 tablespoon of sunflower or olive oil.
Toss until all vegetables are coated in the pink beet juice. Season with a pinch of salt.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving to let the flavors meld.

recipes.title: Shchi (Fresh Cabbage Soup)
recipes.description: One of Russia's most ancient and essential dishes. A light but filling cabbage soup that emphasizes the natural sweetness of fresh vegetables.
instructions: Bring 6 cups of water to a boil. Add the shredded cabbage and potatoes.
Sauté onions in a separate pan until soft, then add to the soup pot.
Add the diced tomatoes and simmer on low for 35 minutes until cabbage is very tender.
Season with bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Serve with fresh parsley.

recipes.title: Ukha (Clear Fish Soup)
recipes.description: A light and clean fish broth that highlights the quality of the ingredients. Historically a favorite of Russian sailors, it is rich in protein and extremely healthy.

ingredients.displayName: Cod or Sea Bass fillets, cubed

instructions: Bring 5 cups of water to a boil. Add diced potatoes and a whole peeled onion.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then add the fish chunks.
Cook gently for 15 more minutes. Remove and discard the whole onion.
Season with salt and whole black peppercorns. Stir in a generous amount of fresh dill before serving.

recipes.title: Roasted Rabbit with Garlic & Herbs
recipes.description: Rabbit is a traditional lean meat in Russian rural cooking. This recipe roasts the meat with garlic and herbs for a high-protein, low-fat alternative to beef.
instructions: Rub the rabbit pieces with crushed garlic, salt, and rosemary.
Place in a baking dish and cover with foil. Bake at 375°F for 40 minutes.
Remove foil and roast for 10 more minutes until golden brown.

recipes.title: Baked Apples with Honey & Berries
recipes.description: A light and healthy traditional Russian dessert. Tart apples are cored and filled with honey, then baked until soft and caramelized.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Core the apples, leaving the bottom intact.
Fill the center of each apple with a mixture of honey and walnuts.
Place in a baking dish with a splash of water. Bake for 20 minutes until tender.

recipes.title: Russian Mushroom Barley Soup
recipes.description: A rustic and filling soup that combines the chewiness of pearl barley with the deep umami of wild mushrooms. High in fiber and very satisfying.
instructions: Soak dried mushrooms for 20 mins if using. Boil barley and potatoes in 6 cups of water.
Sauté chopped mushrooms and onions, then add to the soup pot.
Simmer for 40 minutes until barley is tender and chewy. Season with salt and pepper.

recipes.title: Steamed Zucchini with Fresh Dill
recipes.description: A very simple and clean side dish. Zucchini is steamed gently to preserve its nutrients and then tossed with aromatic Russian dill.
instructions: Steam zucchini rounds for 8-10 minutes until tender.
Toss immediately with fresh dill and a tiny pinch of sea salt.

recipes.title: Lite Olivier Salad with Turkey
recipes.description: A healthy update to the famous 'Russian Salad'. We use lean boiled turkey and high-protein Greek yogurt to create a satisfying and nutrient-dense meal.
instructions: In a large bowl, mix diced turkey, chopped egg, and diced pickles.
Add Greek yogurt and a teaspoon of mustard. Season with plenty of black pepper.
Toss gently until well combined. Serve chilled.

recipes.title: Probiotic Kefir with Herbs
recipes.description: Kefir is a legendary fermented drink in Russia. This savory version is blended with fresh herbs and acts as a powerful aid to digestion.
instructions: Pour kefir into a glass. Stir in the minced dill and grated cucumber. Enjoy cold as a healthy snack.

recipes.title: Okroshka (Cold Summer Soup)
recipes.description: The ultimate Russian summer cooler. A refreshing and low-calorie cold soup made with a base of probiotic kefir and fresh garden vegetables.
instructions: Finely dice the cucumber, radishes, and egg. Place them in a large bowl.
Pour ice-cold kefir over the vegetables. Season with salt and lots of fresh dill.
Mix well and serve immediately while cold.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Onions
recipes.description: A very common and healthy Russian way to prepare white fish. Cod is baked on a bed of sweet onions, which keep the fish moist and flavorful.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with the onion rings.
Place cod on top of the onions. Drizzle with lemon juice and a tiny bit of salt.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until fish is opaque and flaky.

recipes.title: Lean Stuffed Cabbage (Golubtsi)
recipes.description: Traditional cabbage rolls made healthier with lean ground turkey and whole grain brown rice. Simmered in a light tomato sauce.
instructions: Mix ground turkey with brown rice and seasonings.
Place a portion of the meat mixture in each cabbage leaf and roll tightly.
Simmer the rolls in a pot with a cup of tomato puree and 1/2 cup water for 40 minutes over low heat.

recipes.title: Boiled Beef Tongue Platter
recipes.description: A Russian delicacy. High in iron and protein, the tongue is slow-boiled until tender and served thin with sharp horseradish.
instructions: Boil the tongue in water with bay leaves for 2 hours until tender.
Immediately place in cold water to peel off the outer skin. Slice thin and serve cold.

recipes.title: Spring Radish & Chive Salad
recipes.description: A crunchy and peppery salad that marks the beginning of spring in Russia. Low in calories and extremely fresh.
instructions: Toss sliced radishes with chopped chives. Drizzle with a teaspoon of sunflower oil and a pinch of salt.

recipes.title: Stuffed Baked Pumpkin
recipes.description: A rustic and decorative meal. A whole sugar pumpkin is stuffed with a savory mixture of buckwheat and mushrooms, then baked until tender.
instructions: Cut the top off the pumpkin and remove seeds. Fill with a mixture of buckwheat and mushrooms.
Replace the top and bake at 350°F for 60 minutes until the pumpkin flesh is soft.

recipes.title: Lite Mushroom Stroganoff
recipes.description: A vegetarian take on the classic. We use a variety of fresh mushrooms to provide a meaty texture, with a light yogurt sauce.
instructions: Sauté mushrooms and onions until golden. Turn off heat and stir in yogurt and black pepper.
Serve over whole wheat noodles or buckwheat.

recipes.title: Baked Trout with Garlic
recipes.description: Fresh river trout is a staple in many Russian regions. Baked simply with garlic and herbs to maintain its delicate flavor and omega-3 profile.

ingredients.displayName: Fresh rainbow trout, whole or fillet

instructions: Stuff garlic slivers into shallow cuts in the fish. Bake at 375°F for 20 minutes until flaky.

recipes.title: Russian Cabbage & Carrot Slaw
recipes.description: A staple side dish (Vitamin Salad). The cabbage is massaged with salt to tenderize it, creating a crisp and high-fiber accompaniment to any meal.
instructions: Mix shredded cabbage and carrots with a pinch of salt. Massage with your hands until the cabbage softens.
Toss with apple cider vinegar and a drop of oil.

recipes.title: Steel-Cut Oats with Berries
recipes.description: A wholesome and high-fiber start to the day. Steel-cut oats take longer to cook but provide excellent satiety and nutrition.
instructions: Cook oats in 3 cups of water for 25 minutes until tender but still having a 'bite'. Top with fresh berries.

recipes.title: Lite Baked Chicken Kiev
recipes.description: A much lighter version of the buttery classic. We use a small amount of herb butter and bake the chicken instead of deep-frying it.
instructions: Flatten chicken breasts. Place a small piece of herb butter inside and roll tightly.
Secure with toothpicks and bake at 400°F for 25 minutes until golden and cooked through.

recipes.title: Probiotic Sauerkraut (Kvashenaya Kapusta)
recipes.description: Traditional Russian fermented cabbage. Naturally rich in probiotics and Vitamin C, it is a vital part of the winter diet in Russia.
instructions: Shred the cabbage and mix with salt. Massage for 10 mins until juice is released.
Pack tightly into a glass jar and let sit at room temp for 3-5 days to ferment.

recipes.title: Russian Egg & Dill Salad
recipes.description: A light and high-protein salad. Hard-boiled eggs are mashed with fresh dill and a touch of yogurt for a healthy lunch option.
instructions: Mash the eggs in a bowl. Stir in the dill and yogurt. Season with salt and pepper.
